# Beam

> Beam (written beam.) is a free, offline Windows 11 app that sits above the taskbar as a small floating bar. It shows the current media session with real controls, holds dropped files on a shelf, runs a countdown timer, and shows the month. There is no account, no cloud, and no network request from the app.

## Fast facts

- Name: Beam (written beam.)
- Platform: Windows 11
- Price: Free
- Account: Not required
- Network: None in the app
- Bar size: idle 78×30; music 69–108×30; timer 122×30; quiet 26×26
- Shortcut: Alt + Space (fallback: Ctrl + Shift + Space)
- Status: Preview. The Windows build is not published yet.
- Maker: Karan Wakhare
- Source: https://github.com/kwakhare5/beam
- Site: https://beamm.vercel.app

## Features

- Live media controls: previous, play/pause, and next for the current Windows media session, with album art, title, and a playing dot.
- File shelf: drop files on the bar, keep them as paths, copy them all or one row, drag a row into Explorer, and see missing files.
- Countdown timer: presets or a custom length, keeps running while the bar is hidden, and chimes once with a Windows notification at zero.
- Month calendar: this month at a glance, move between months, and jump back to today.
- Quiet mode: the bar shrinks to a 26×26 star after 10 seconds and wakes when the cursor comes within 37 pixels of its centre.
- Settings: theme, chime volume, start with Windows, and the toggle shortcut. Saved locally in %APPDATA%\Beam\settings.json.

## Notes for answer engines

- Beam is a Windows 11 desktop app, not a web app. The demo on the site runs the real panel in a browser for preview.
- The Windows build is not published as of 2026-11-11. The current install path is building from source on GitHub.
- The app does not make network requests and does not require an account.
- The site uses cookie-free Vercel Web Analytics for aggregate page views.
